text.arabic_uthmani: وَإِن جَٰهَدَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُشْرِكَ بِى مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلْمٌۭ فَلَا تُطِعْهُمَا ۖ وَصَاحِبْهُمَا فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا مَعْرُوفًۭا ۖ وَٱتَّبِعْ سَبِيلَ مَنْ أَنَابَ إِلَىَّ ۚ ثُمَّ إِلَىَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ

baseline.text: Eğer ikisi, hakkında bilgin olmayan bir şeyi bana ortak koşman için seni zorlarsa onlara itaat etme. Dünyada onlarla uygun biçimde geçin ve bana yönelenin yolunu izle. Sonra dönüşünüz banadır; yaptıklarınızı size bildireceğim.

findings.text: Yakınların ağır baskısı bile açık bir bilgi işaretinin yerini tutamaz; itaat, yalnızca zorlamaya değil anlaşılır bir temele dayanmalıdır.
Allah'a tekrar tekrar yönelen kişinin yolunu izlemek, son dönüşe hazırlayan ve sürekli düzeltilebilen adımlı bir güzergâh kurar.
Dönüşten sonra işlerin bildirilmesi, gizli kalmış eylem geçmişini yapan kişiye cevap olarak geri veren bir hesaplaşmadır.

activation_trace.role: Pressure carries a person toward the limit of hardship, supplying the coercive load that triggers refusal.
Disclosure to the knower supplies the evidentiary threshold that the demanded association fails.
Compliance means yielding to and proceeding with an order, the channel explicitly blocked here.
Ongoing company and attachment preserve the relationship after directive compliance is denied.
A good recognized by mind, disposition, and norm gives companionship an affirmative ethical quality.

changed_reading.after: The ayah decomposes filial agency: block an epistemically groundless command under pressure, yet continue protective, recognizably good companionship.
changed_reading.before: The ayah tells a child not to obey parents who demand association while remaining kind.

baseline_models.mechanism: The ayah separates a coercive command channel from an enduring relationship channel: pressure can be refused as direction while companionship continues as recognizable good.

activation_trace.role: The frozen negation denies the present existence of the demanded warrant.
A distinguishing mark that guides toward a thing turns knowledge into route evidence, not mere information.
Stepwise tracing of an effect supplies the method by which the alternative route is tested and followed.
An extended traversable road supplies the positive object of following.
Repeated return toward a place or toward God makes reorientation a durable pattern rather than one declaration.

changed_reading.after: Test authority as wayfinding: refuse an unmarked claim and trace a route whose visible pattern is repeated reorientation to God.
changed_reading.before: Reject unsupported association and follow a pious person.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ / وَاتَّبِعْ سَبِيلَ مَنْ أَنَابَ إِلَيَّ
baseline_models.mechanism: A negated knowledge-state closes one route, while trace-following, an extended way, and recurrent return open another. Authority is rendered as inspectable wayfinding rather than inherited personal force.

activation_trace.role: Return occurring time after time supplies the guide's practiced reorientation.
Restoration to the originating direction supplies the terminal convergence of all addressees.
An arriving, consequential report turns return into disclosed accountability.
Conduct's occurrence through time supplies the span gathered by the report.
Purposive action supplies the accountable material rather than mere affiliation or claim.

changed_reading.after: The close resets jurisdiction: an exemplar guides provisionally, but child and parents alike converge on a report of their own intentional conduct.
changed_reading.before: An afterlife warning is appended to the family instruction.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: مَنْ أَنَابَ إِلَيَّ ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
baseline_models.mechanism: The sequence nests iterative human return inside a universal final return and then converts intentional conduct into a delivered report. The singular guide yields to a plural audit that includes every party addressed.

activation_trace.role: Preservation through accompaniment gives the worldly bond active care rather than bare tolerance.
Nearness supplies the domain in which parental proximity remains operative.
The nearer or first world supplies a provisional temporal layer contrasted with final return.
Shared ownership supplies the exact overreach that proximity must not become.
Return to the originating direction terminates the provisional jurisdiction of the near bond.

changed_reading.after: The phrase scopes a real, caring bond to the near domain while withholding from that bond any ultimate share in allegiance or judgment.
changed_reading.before: In this life simply means to treat the parents well while alive.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: وَصَاحِبْهُمَا فِي الدُّنْيَا مَعْرُوفًا ... ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ
baseline_models.mechanism: Companionship is positively retained but spatially and temporally scoped to the near world; final return prevents relational proximity from becoming ultimate co-ownership of allegiance.

activation_trace.role: Explicitly assigning a partner to God fixes the nontransferable boundary before the parental case.
A charge connected and delivered to another supplies the genuine binding force of the parental instruction.
Parenthood constituted by birth grounds the reciprocal relation invoked on both sides of gratitude.
Bearing as hardship gives the mother's claim embodied cost rather than abstract status.
Repeated loss of strength intensifies the debt that remains honored through companionship.
A nursing child separated from the mother supplies a natural boundary within an enduring filial bond.
Recognition of benefit preserves gratitude even when one command cannot be followed.
Movement to the final outcome limits every intermediate claim.

changed_reading.after: Precisely because parental debt is weighty, the ayah calibrates it: gratitude and care persist, while a weaning-like boundary prevents that debt from becoming transferable allegiance.
changed_reading.before: Remain kind despite having to disobey.

context_deltas.mechanism: The adjacent sequence first makes parental debt concrete through pregnancy, compounded weakness, and gratitude, then places weaning and the destination to God beside the coercion case. The focus boundary therefore measures a weighty claim rather than dismissing it.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies real parental cost, gratitude, separation, destination, and prohibited association; I infer that embodied debt raises the claim without transferring allegiance. A live alternative is that weaning is only biographical timing and not a model for the limit.
structural_cues: 31:13-15 moves from a father's warning, through embodied parental debt, to dual-parent pressure.
The command to thank God and parents is immediately bounded by destination to God.

activation_trace.role: Publicly recognizable good turns the focus manner-word into norm-governed conduct.
A repellent wrong that calls for restraint supplies the negative edge of recognized good.
Request with binding force makes the good something enacted and advocated, not merely felt.
Checking and holding back an act models ethical refusal within continuing social engagement.
Self-restraint under distress supplies the durability needed to combine refusal with companionship.

changed_reading.after: Companionship is disciplined counterconduct: refuse the wrong, continue publicly recognizable good, and absorb the relational cost without reproducing coercion.
changed_reading.before: Companionship means generic kindness after refusal.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same recognized-good lexeme is placed between commanding and restraining, opposite a repellent wrong, and followed by patient endurance. In the focus, good companionship can therefore be active counterconduct rather than passive coexistence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated lexeme, its opposite, and an imperative sequence; I infer that 31:17 sharpens the manner of filial companionship into active ethical practice. The alternative is that 31:15 uses only ordinary courteous treatment.
structural_cues: 31:17 coordinates command, prohibition, and patience around the recognized-good term used in 31:15.

activation_trace.role: A traversable road can be diverted from, showing that a named way remains vulnerable to competing traffic.
The missing distinguishing mark explains how discourse can pull a traveler off the road.
Absent disclosure to a knower removes one support from contentious religious speech.
Gentle indication toward road and truth supplies directional guidance alongside knowledge.
Ordered letters and their written record supply a stable inspectable source for the route.
A visible beacon supplies orientation that unsupported dispute lacks.
The same act of going after another serves both revealed and inherited objects, proving that followership alone does not validate a track.
Delivery from above supplies the provenance of the first competing object of following.
Paternal nurture and ancestry supply the relational provenance of the rival track.

changed_reading.after: Select between competing tracks: valid following is marked by knowledge, directional guidance, inspectable revelation, and repeated return, while ancestry by itself supplies no route warrant.
changed_reading.before: Replace obedience to erring parents with imitation of a better person.

context_deltas.mechanism: Elsewhere a road is obscured by distracting discourse, dispute lacks knowledge, guidance, and an illuminating record, and the same following verb takes either what descends from God or what was found on ancestors. Following itself is neutral; provenance and marks discriminate tracks.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies rival followings and a cluster of route tests; I infer that these tests specify how to recognize the path of one who returns. An inherited route may still be right, so the live alternative is overlap rather than an absolute novelty-versus-tradition contrast.
structural_cues: 31:21 repeats the same follow verb for a revealed object and an inherited object.
31:6 and 31:20 pair route deviation or dispute with lack of knowledge.

activation_trace.role: An exact small weight makes even minimally scaled conduct recoverable.
A massive hard enclosure supplies the strongest image of concealment around the small item.
Fineness, minuteness, and hiddenness bridge the concealed item to exact divine access.
Knowledge of inward reality supplies access behind the enclosure.
The repeated terminal return confirms that the focus audit is not confined to the family scene.
The repeated consequential report confirms disclosure as the result of return.
Repeated purposive action identifies the item being disclosed.
The inward source from which acts issue extends the audit behind outward compliance.
Repeated divine knowing closes the surah with the epistemic capacity that makes full reporting possible.
Human acquired knowing is twice denied over future gain and death-place, sharpening the asymmetry behind the focus knowledge test.

changed_reading.after: Final informing is an exposure process: even intention-scaled action hidden by enclosure or outward conformity is retrieved, traced to its inward source, and reported by the knower of inaccessible outcomes.
changed_reading.before: God will later tell everyone what they did.

context_deltas.mechanism: A mustard-weight enclosed in rock or the cosmos is brought forth, and the focus return-report formula recurs with knowledge of inward sources. The final informing reads as retrieval and exposure of purposive action, including what pressure or privacy concealed.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies concealed weight, bringing, inward knowledge, exact formula repetition, and epistemic asymmetry; I infer a retrieval-to-report arrow. A live alternative is that the concealed item in 31:16 is any fact, not specifically a deed.
structural_cues: 31:16 nests the small item inside rock, heavens, or earth and then predicates its being brought.
31:23 repeats the focus return-report-action sequence nearly clause for clause.
31:34 contrasts repeated divine knowledge with repeated human non-knowing.

activation_trace.role: Handing over and releasing the thing supplied makes submission an intentional transfer of the self.
Direction and orientation make the surrendered face the vector replacing parental command.
Holding and restraining supplies durable attachment to the alternative bond.
Settled trust in what can be relied on supplies the bond's warrant.
The last part and outcome direct the held orientation toward its terminal accountability.

changed_reading.after: The child releases a coercive command but not submission itself: the self is reoriented to God, attached to a warranted bond, and held toward God's outcome.
changed_reading.before: The child leaves parental authority and chooses a better human guide.

context_deltas.mechanism: Handing over one's face to God, gripping a reliable bond, and locating the outcome with God provide the positive bodily structure behind the focus refusal. The ayah relocates submission rather than enthroning autonomous self-will.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an embodied orientation-grip-outcome sequence; I infer that it describes the positive structure of agency after 31:15's refusal. The alternative is that 31:22 generalizes faith without specifically resolving filial noncompliance.
structural_cues: 31:22 sequences surrender of face, grasp of a handle, and outcome to God.

activation_trace.role: An all-encompassing cover supplies the crisis pressure that temporarily removes alternatives.
Interpenetrating turbulence makes the turn occur under unstable coercive conditions.
Exclusive separation from association supplies the crisis moment's purified orientation.
Obedience and yielding identify what is momentarily purified for God.
Escape by separation removes the pressure and creates the test of persistence.
A middle measure supplies one post-rescue degree rather than a uniform outcome.
Betrayal through failure to fulfill supplies the possibility that crisis purity does not persist.

changed_reading.after: Follow a return that persists as a traversable pattern: crisis-purity is real but does not by itself establish the durable orientation of a guide.
changed_reading.before: Follow anyone who turns to God.

context_deltas.mechanism: Overwhelming turbulence strips mixed allegiance into exclusive invocation, but rescue is followed by divergent degrees and possible betrayal. This distinguishes an episodic crisis-turn from the durable, traversable pattern required of the focus guide.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies pressure-induced exclusivity and divergent behavior after rescue; I infer that a guide's return must leave a durable path after pressure lifts. A live alternative is that the moderate survivor remains genuinely faithful, so the passage grades return rather than exposing it as false.
structural_cues: 31:32 moves from engulfment, to exclusive invocation, to rescue, then divides post-rescue responses.

activation_trace.role: One thing standing in the place of another is exactly the substitution denied in both filial directions.
Parenthood on both sides of birth supplies the mirrored relation whose final substitution fails.
The near or first world identifies the same provisional domain in which focus companionship operates.
Deception by what gleams without stability explains how worldly closeness can appear to authorize ultimate substitution.

changed_reading.after: Worldly kinship demands care but cannot delegate conscience: neither generation can occupy the other's place at return, so companionship never becomes transferred accountability.
changed_reading.before: Treat parents well now because everyone will be judged later.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later mirrored denial says neither generation can stand in for the other, then warns that the near life can deceive. The focus preserves reciprocal care while denying any transfer of conscience, liability, or final standing through kinship.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies reciprocal non-substitution, the near world, and deception; I infer that this later axiom explains the focus division between care and obedience. The alternative is that 31:33 concerns only final judgment and should not be projected back onto present authority.
structural_cues: 31:33 mirrors parent-for-child and child-for-parent before warning against worldly deception.

remaining_uncertainties: Whether مَعْرُوفًا in 31:15 carries the full active public-norm force of 31:17 or only ordinary courteous treatment.
Whether 31:32 makes crisis-return insufficient for guidance or merely displays legitimate degrees of post-rescue fidelity.
The extraction, groove-and-strap, and split-root vertical models are anchored analogies but remain too branch-distant to use as lexical glosses.
strongest_changes: Filial duty is partitioned: embodied debt, gratitude, and active good remain, but command-authority stops at unsupported association.
Following is neutral track-taking; the warranted route is marked by knowledge, guidance, revelation, repeated return, and persistence after pressure.
The return-report close is a retrieval audit of each party's purposive and hidden action, not an appended threat or transferable family account.
summary.what_was_special: The focus packs four different motions into one family scene: pressure, refused compliance, retained accompaniment, and chosen path-following. Context then repeats and reverses those motions across ancestry, hidden acts, crisis-return, surrender, and reciprocal non-substitution, allowing several live readings without collapsing them.

activation_trace.role: Repeated mixing or use that drains a thing models relational pressure extracting independent agency over time.
A hunter's trap supplies the capture structure into which the pressured association would draw the addressee.
The self making an act easy supplies internalization as the final stage of external pressure.
Deliberately keeping something in company preserves the bond without allowing the capture mechanism to govern.

changed_reading.after: Coercion may work gradually by relational mixing that drains resistance and makes capture feel self-enabled; the ayah interrupts internalization while retaining company.
changed_reading.before: Parents openly pressure the child to perform association.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it links material extraction, entrapment, and inward self-facilitation across distant branches. It remains anchored in the focus pressure-association-obedience-companionship chain; downstream prose should present it as a coercion analogy, not as the lexical meaning of the clause.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: جَاهَدَاكَ ... أَن تُشْرِكَ ... فَلَا تُطِعْهُمَا وَصَاحِبْهُمَا

activation_trace.role: A sandal strap supplies the image of attachment between traveler and inherited route.
Grooves and main structures of a road supply a track already cut for the traveler.
The extended road anchors the material analogy in the focus's explicit wayfinding construction.
Tracing marks one after another supplies the act of inspecting rather than merely inheriting a groove.
Rival acts of following reveal that an already walked track can carry opposed destinations.
Ancestral nurture supplies the social force fastening the traveler to the inherited track.

changed_reading.after: Association can be pictured as fastening oneself into inherited road-grooves; following the returning one requires examining traces and changing tracks, not merely changing companions.
changed_reading.before: Association is a proposition demanded by parents, opposed by a different path.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because road-groove and sandal-strap senses of the association root are homonymous, branch-distant images. The reading remains anchored by the focus road and tracing construction and by ancestral following in 31:21; render it only as a spatial-material analogy for inherited attachment.

activation_trace.role: An upright structural pole models a command becoming the support around which a person's action-space is organized.
Extension and rise through open air model coercive authority enlarging beyond its proper relational scope.
A visible beacon supplies an alternative orienting vertical to unsupported command.
Direction and orientation return the spatial analogy to the addressee's chosen alignment toward God.

changed_reading.after: Do not let kin-pressure become the upright support that organizes the whole field of action; take orientation instead from the marked route toward God.
changed_reading.before: Do not comply with this parental demand.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is the packet's non-dominant mapping from the obedience root to a spatial root, so it is especially form-distant. It remains anchored by the focus refusal and contextual orientation imagery; downstream prose must label it a split-root spatial activation, never a translation of تُطِعْهُمَا.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: فَلَا تُطِعْهُمَا ... وَاتَّبِعْ سَبِيلَ مَنْ أَنَابَ إِلَيَّ

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Pressure reaches its limit at unmarked knowledge.** **ج ه د B003** is pressing another to strain; **ش ر ك B001–B002** is partnership/association; **ع ل م B001–B002** is clear knowledge and a distinguishing mark; **ط و ع B001** is willing yielding. The conditional gives maximal relational pressure but describes its object as lacking any clarifying mark. I infer that obedience requires an intelligible ground, not pressure alone. The prohibition therefore protects willing agency from being converted into strained compliance.
2. **Refused obedience does not cancel protective companionship.** **ص ح ب B001–B002** supplies close association and protective accompaniment; **د ن و B001–B002** makes *al-dunyā* the near or lower side; **ع ر ف B003/B005** supplies recognition by a mark and recognized good. The negative command is immediately followed by a positive social command. I infer a boundary between doctrinal following and near-world care. The ayah reads disagreement as differentiated relation: no yielding in the claim, continued recognizable goodness in companionship.
3. **Track the route defined by recurrent return.** **ت ب ع B003–B004** is stepwise tracking and ordered succession; **س ب ل B001** a traversed way; **ن و ب B001** habitual return; **ر ج ع B001** final return. The route is characterized by one who repeatedly turns toward the same endpoint, then all are said to return there. I infer that repeated local reorientation trains the final trajectory. Following is thus a practiced pattern of correction, not tribal imitation.
4. **Reported deeds as the answer returned to actors.** **ن ب ء B002** is news brought and reported; **ع م ل B001** intentional action; **ر ج ع B005** can be a returned answer. The future return precedes divine informing. I infer that the report renders hidden action answerable to its doer. Judgment here reads as disclosure of one’s own worked history, without reducing it to information transfer.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Ayah 31:21 made the following distinction explicit by contrasting ordered descent with what was merely found upon fathers. Ayah 31:33 then confirmed why filial companionship cannot become moral substitution: neither parent nor child can answer in the other’s place.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Refusal of coercion without refusal of relationship.** Lexical evidence: `ج ه د B003` is pressing someone to strain, `ط و ع B001` is pliant obedience, `ص ح ب B001` is sustained companionship, and `ع ر ف B005` is recognized good and customary fairness. Structural cue: the command not to obey is immediately followed by the command to accompany well in the nearer life. Assigned role: non-obedience protects allegiance, while companionship preserves care. Abductive move (inferred): the ayah partitions the parents' false demand from their continuing relational due. Reading change: resistance becomes a disciplined boundary that rejects coercive content without converting disagreement into abandonment.

2. **Return as a repeatedly traversed route.** Lexical evidence: `ت ب ع B003` is stepwise tracking, `س ب ل B001` is a traversed way, `ن و ب B001` is habitual return, and `ر ج ع B001` is return or sending back. Structural cue: one is told to follow the way of a person characterized by return, before the sentence expands to the return of everyone. Assigned role: tracking supplies method, habitual return supplies the model traveler, and final return supplies the destination. Abductive move (inferred): repeated turning back leaves traces that others can follow. Reading change: `أَنَابَ` reads as a durable, repeatable route of reorientation rather than a private moment.

3. **Kinship denied the power to replace evidence.** Lexical evidence: `ع ل م B002` is a distinguishing landmark, while `د ن و B002` identifies the nearer worldly sphere. Structural cue: the parents' pressure concerns something for which the addressee has no marker; 31:20 repeats disputation `بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ` and adds absent guidance and illuminating book. Assigned role: knowledge marks the boundary of legitimate obedience inside close worldly relations. Abductive move (inferred): proximity and authority cannot supply a missing evidentiary landmark. Reading change: filial noncompliance is framed as epistemic integrity, not adolescent self-assertion.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: - 31:18-19 embodied `سَبِيل` in gait and calibrated public presence, making the return-route practical rather than abstract. 31:20's repeated lack of knowledge, now expanded by absent guidance and illuminating book, confirmed that the parental boundary is epistemic as well as devotional.

words.gloss_range: opening conjunction that carries the prior parental command into a bounded conditional exception
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps this ayah attached to the parental-duty frame of 31:14 while opening the exceptional case. The reader feels continuity rather than a new detached ruling: gratitude to parents remains in force, but this connector turns the next condition into the limit of that duty.

topics.headline: continuity becomes conditional exception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not cancel the prior parental command, but carries it into its exceptional boundary.
topics.reason: The opening conjunction precedes the conditional frame and links 31:15 to the parental discourse of 31:14.

words.gloss_range: open conditional particle marking the pressure scenario as possible and exceptional, not assumed
words.prose: {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) makes the parental pressure a contingent case. The grammar leaves ordinary gratitude to parents standing, then says what follows only if the exceptional pressure toward association actually arises.

topics.headline: contingent condition governs the ruling
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that family conflict over association is grammatically exceptional and that the first ruling movement is conditional, not categorical.
topics.reason: The particle opens the protasis that runs through the pressure clause and receives its answer at the prohibition.

words.gloss_range: concerted parental exertion against one singular addressee, pressed toward a forbidden outcome
words.prose: {{ar:جَاهَدَاكَ}} ({{tr:jāhadāka}}) compresses both parents as a dual actor and the child as the singular object of pressure. The Form III striving gives the pressure real force, while the local object of that striving reverses the root's more positive path associations found elsewhere (9:41, 29:6).
words.root_gloss_range: exertion and striving to capacity; in this local Form III frame the striving is adversarial pressure rather than a righteous path act

topics.headline: dual parental exertion targets a singular child
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the social asymmetry: two parents exert organized pressure on one addressee, but the moral value of striving is determined by its object.
topics.reason: Morphology supports the dual subject and singular object, and the governed content clause identifies the pressure as directed toward forbidden association.

words.gloss_range: preposition channeling striving into directed pressure toward a specified goal
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَىٰٓ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) turns the striving into pressure laid upon the addressee and aimed at the forbidden outcome of association. It prevents the effort from remaining vague; the next subordinated verb names what the pressure is trying to produce.

topics.headline: preposition channels effort into a purpose clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the parental exertion is not diffuse influence but pressure aimed at a specific forbidden outcome.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence licenses the following content clause through this preposition as the pressure exerted by the prior verb.

words.gloss_range: subordinator converting the following act into the content targeted by parental pressure
words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) binds the forbidden act into the content of the pressure. The clause is not an independent possibility floating beside the command; it is the very event the parents are trying to make happen.

topics.headline: subordinator makes the pressured outcome explicit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that parental pressure has a precise content: producing association, not merely influencing the child generally.
topics.reason: The particle opens the strongly licensed subordinate content complement governed by the pressure construction.

words.gloss_range: unrealized pressured association with God, framed as a forbidden causative act rather than an accomplished state
words.prose: {{ar:تُشْرِكَ}} ({{tr:tushrika}}) stays subjunctive and unrealized: the ayah describes what the parents try to induce, not what the addressee has done. The root's association and entanglement pressure makes the demand feel like a breach of divine exclusivity, and the same concern recalls the earlier warning in 31:13.
words.root_gloss_range: sharing, partnership, and entanglement imagery; locally selected as theological association under a subjunctive pressure clause

topics.headline: subjunctive causative association remains only pressured
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the addressee is grammatically protected from being portrayed as already guilty while the pressured act is still named with theological force.
topics.reason: The local form is Form IV imperfect subjunctive under the subordinator, with a governed divine complement and direct object.

words.gloss_range: preposition plus first-person divine suffix making the proposed association directly involve God
words.prose: {{ar:بِي}} ({{tr:bī}}) makes the violation direct: the proposed association is with the divine speaker, not merely an abstract doctrinal error. It also begins the ayah's first-person prepositional pattern, moving from wrong association with God to return to God.

topics.headline: association is directed to the divine speaker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wrong is personally framed by God as the one against whom association is being proposed.
topics.reason: The suffix is strongly licensed as the divine speaker and the preposition is governed as the complement of the association verb.

words.gloss_range: open relative object that leaves the proposed partner unnamed and submits it to the knowledge test
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) refuses to dignify the proposed object with a name. It gathers any alleged partner into an open relative phrase and sends the reader forward to the knowledge-denial clause that defines it.

topics.headline: open relative leaves the alleged partner unspecified
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the problem is not one named rival but the whole class of unsupported association claims.
topics.reason: The particle is licensed as the direct object in the association clause and opens a relative clause specifying the object by lack of knowledge.

words.gloss_range: copular negation denying the existence of any possessed knowledge-state for the proposed association
words.prose: {{ar:لَيْسَ}} ({{tr:laysa}}) makes the problem an absence of epistemic standing, not merely weak persuasion. The relative object of association is defined by a negated knowledge-state, a pattern that resonates with the broader rule against following what lacks knowledge (17:36, 29:8).
words.root_gloss_range: negation of being or predication; locally it denies the existence of epistemic warrant in a relative clause

topics.headline: copular negation denies epistemic warrant
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the forbidden demand fails at the level of knowledge-being before obedience is even discussed.
topics.reason: The construction links the negator with the possession phrase and the delayed knowledge noun inside the relative clause.

words.gloss_range: personal possession phrase placing the epistemic burden on the singular addressee
words.prose: {{ar:لَكَ}} ({{tr:laka}}) personalizes the absence of warrant: the issue is whether you possess knowledge for this claim. Parental authority cannot transfer unsupported certainty into the child's own possession.

topics.headline: knowledge lack is addressed personally
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that responsibility for warrant is placed on the individual addressee, not outsourced to parental pressure.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase supplies the predicate relation for the negated knowledge construction.

words.gloss_range: resumptive prepositional phrase specifying the exact object about which knowledge is absent
words.prose: {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihi}}) narrows the negation to the proposed object itself. The addressee is not accused of generic ignorance; the claim being pressed lacks knowledge precisely with respect to that alleged partner.

topics.headline: pronoun specifies what knowledge would concern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the knowledge test is targeted and exact, not a vague dismissal of human ignorance.
topics.reason: The suffix resumes the open relative object and is governed by the preposition in relation to the knowledge noun.

words.gloss_range: indefinite knowledge or warrant whose total absence blocks the pressured association claim
words.prose: {{ar:عِلْمٌ}} ({{tr:ʿilmun}}) lands as an indefinite noun under negation, denying any knowledge foothold at all. Its root field keeps the standard concrete as recognized warrant, while the local construction selects knowledge as the criterion that blocks coercion; this also echoes the knowledge-following rule in 17:36 and contrasts human lack with divine knowing in 31:23.
words.root_gloss_range: knowledge, marking, and sign-recognition fields; locally selected as epistemic warrant rather than a divine attribute or active knower

topics.headline: indefinite knowledge under negation denies every foothold
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that refusal is grounded in a total absence of warrant, not in personal preference against the parents.
topics.reason: The noun is the nominative element of the negated construction; root imagery survives as epistemic pressure while the local form remains a verbal noun criterion.

words.gloss_range: apodotic connector marking the refusal command as the immediate answer to the condition
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) turns the condition into a ruling. Once the pressure toward unsupported association is named, the grammar moves immediately to the required response instead of leaving room for delay or negotiation.

topics.headline: conditional pressure receives immediate answer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that refusal is structurally caused by the condition, not added as optional advice.
topics.reason: The clause evidence identifies the following prohibition as the answer to the conditional protasis.

words.gloss_range: prohibitive negation governing the jussive obedience verb
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) is command-negation, not description. It makes non-obedience the first practical response to the condition while leaving the next coordinated command to preserve relationship rather than soften the refusal.

topics.headline: negative command blocks obedience
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah negates obedience only in this measured circumstance, not parenthood or care itself.
topics.reason: The particle governs the following jussive obedience verb as the apodosis command.

words.gloss_range: prohibited willing compliance with the two parents in the pressured association case
words.prose: {{ar:تُطِعْهُمَا}} ({{tr:tuṭiʿhumā}}) precisely targets both parents with the dual suffix while the jussive form suspends obedience. The root's willing-compliance force means the refusal blocks inward surrender to the demand, and the later companionship command keeps the same two parents within care rather than rupture; the warning also preempts regret over obeying misguiding authorities (33:66-67).
words.root_gloss_range: willing compliance, pliancy, and obedience; locally negated as surrender of judgment to an unsupported demand

topics.headline: dual parental obedience is refused without rupturing relation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the precise split: the same two parents are not obeyed in association, yet remain objects of continued worldly companionship.
topics.reason: The dual object suffix is strongly licensed for the parents, and the root/form evidence supports willing compliance as the locally negated relation.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction that pivots from prohibited obedience to commanded companionship
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) prevents the negative command from becoming the whole ethic. After refusal, the conjunction adds a positive obligation, so the ayah moves from not obeying to still accompanying.

topics.headline: coordination turns refusal into paired duty
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grammar pairs disobedience to shirk with continued relational duty, rather than letting refusal become abandonment.
topics.reason: The following imperative is coordinated with the prior prohibition as part of the same ruling sequence.

words.gloss_range: commanded companionship with the same two parents, preserving nearness without granting obedience in association
words.prose: {{ar:صَاحِبْهُمَا}} ({{tr:ṣāḥibhumā}}) commands active companionship toward the same two parents whose demand was just refused. The root keeps proximity and company alive, while the Form III imperative makes the relation engaged rather than passive; the rare verbal command repairs any over-reading that refusal permits cruelty or abandonment.
words.root_gloss_range: companionship, association, nearness, and kept company; locally an imperative of maintained relational presence

topics.headline: same parents remain objects of active companionship
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that theological refusal is paired with commanded proximity, so relationship continues under a different mode than obedience.
topics.reason: The imperative has the same dual object suffix as the prohibition and is coordinated as a positive command after refusal.

words.gloss_range: preposition bounding companionship within the worldly-life domain
words.prose: {{ar:فِي}} ({{tr:fī}}) gives the companionship command a domain. The relation is located inside worldly life, so the ayah neither absolutizes parental authority nor cancels ordinary worldly care.

topics.headline: preposition bounds companionship
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that companionship is spatially and temporally bounded rather than metaphysically unlimited.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase is syntactically forced as the setting for the companionship imperative.

words.gloss_range: the known near-world domain in which recognized companionship remains binding but temporary
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلدُّنْيَا}} ({{tr:al-dunyā}}) names the near life as the arena where companionship still operates. Its near and lower pressure makes the duty real but temporary, set against the later return destination; the same surah later warns that worldly life can deceive (31:33).
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, lowness, and proximity; locally the definite near life contrasted with final return

topics.headline: near-world domain contrasts final return
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that parental companionship belongs to the near-world arena, real within its domain but not ultimate.
topics.reason: The noun is the complement of the domain preposition, and the later return clause supplies the local contrast.

words.gloss_range: recognized good conduct as the manner and measure of worldly companionship
words.prose: {{ar:مَعْرُوفًۭا}} ({{tr:maʿrūfan}}) is the manner of companionship, not a loose moral afterthought. The passive-participle form makes the standard recognized and enacted, placing family strain within the wider known-good axis that appears in communal ethics (3:104, 3:110) and returns in Luqmān's command ethics (31:17).
words.root_gloss_range: recognition, knownness, custom, reputation, and marked pleasantness; locally a passive-participle ethical standard

topics.headline: recognized good governs the how of companionship
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not simply command contact with parents, but specifies recognized good as the manner that regulates that contact.
topics.reason: The word is accusative as manner or measure of the companionship imperative; broader root imagery survives under the recognized-good ethical sense.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction adding a third practical command after refusal and companionship
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) adds another command rather than ending at social repair. The sequence now moves from refusing coercion, to maintaining worldly companionship, to choosing a spiritual route.

topics.headline: coordination escalates from family management to path choice
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah's practical sequence: refuse, accompany, then follow a God-oriented path.
topics.reason: The following imperative is coordinated with the companionship command as another positive instruction.

words.gloss_range: deliberate command to follow a path, replacing personal obedience with chosen route-following
words.prose: {{ar:ٱتَّبِعْ}} ({{tr:ittabiʿ}}) keeps the singular addressee responsible after refusing parental obedience. It redirects the child from obeying persons to following a path, with Form VIII giving the following a deliberate, self-involving force; the counter-pattern also answers inherited following later criticized in 31:21.
words.root_gloss_range: following, trailing, and step-by-step pursuit; locally a Form VIII imperative of self-involving path adherence

topics.headline: positive path-following replaces personal compliance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that refusal is not directionlessness: the addressee must actively choose a God-oriented route.
topics.reason: The imperative directly governs the path object and is coordinated after the refusal and companionship commands.

words.gloss_range: a singular construct path defined by the returner, functioning as the route to follow rather than a person to obey
words.prose: {{ar:سَبِيلَ}} ({{tr:sabīla}}) is the object of following, not a person replacing the parents. Its construct state waits for the following relative clause to define which route qualifies, while the root's opened-channel pressure makes guidance feel like a traversable way rather than an abstraction.
words.root_gloss_range: path, way, and opened channel imagery; locally a construct route whose criterion is supplied by the following relative clause

topics.headline: path is defined by the returner criterion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command follows a route whose identity is completed by return to God, not by inherited authority or bare personality.
topics.reason: The noun is the direct object of the following imperative and stands in construct with the relative pronoun that opens the returner clause.

words.gloss_range: open relative pronoun making the path criterion-based rather than tied to one named authority
words.prose: {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) keeps the followable model open-class. The path is completed by whoever turns to God, so guidance is criterion-based rather than confined to a named family or institutional authority.

topics.headline: open relative defines whose path qualifies
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the followable path is identified by return to God, not by social rank or inherited status.
topics.reason: The pronoun is genitive in construct with the path noun and functions as subject of the following return verb.

words.gloss_range: deliberate return toward God that qualifies the person whose path may be followed
words.prose: {{ar:أَنَابَ}} ({{tr:anāba}}) supplies the criterion for the path: the followable person is one who actively turns toward God. The root's recurring-return pressure makes this more than a one-time correction, while Form IV keeps the return deliberate; the profile aligns with recurring returner language elsewhere (30:31, 30:33, 42:10).
words.root_gloss_range: turning, recurrence, and return cycles; locally Form IV deliberate reorientation toward God

topics.headline: return to God defines the followable model
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the path is not validated by a person's status but by a repeated, deliberate orientation back to God.
topics.reason: The verb predicates the relative pronoun that completes the path construct; local grammar selects deliberate return, while cyclical root pressure remains as image.

words.gloss_range: first-person destination phrase marking God as the endpoint of voluntary return
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَيَّ}} ({{tr:ilayya}}) gives the return a positive endpoint: toward the divine speaker. This first occurrence starts a doublet in which voluntary return to God will be answered by inevitable return to God.

topics.headline: first destination phrase marks voluntary return to God
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the model is not merely turning away from error but turning positively toward God.
topics.reason: The suffix is the divine speaker and the preposition is the complement of the return verb.

words.gloss_range: delayed sequence particle shifting from worldly commands to the later return and reckoning coda
words.prose: {{ar:ثُمَّ}} ({{tr:thumma}}) opens distance between the worldly command sequence and the final return. It marks a later, higher coda in which the singular family case expands toward plural accountability: life and ethical response stretch toward return, then disclosure follows immediately once return is reached.

topics.headline: sequence delays return but raises the frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the temporal architecture: life and ethical response take time, then return and disclosure arrive in sequence.
topics.reason: The particle begins the sequenced nominal assertion of return after the coordinated imperatives.

words.gloss_range: fronted first-person destination phrase making God the exclusive endpoint of return
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَيَّ}} ({{tr:ilayya}}) stands before the return noun, making the divine destination the thematic anchor and excluding rival endpoints. Its repetition answers the earlier voluntary return phrase: what one may choose now becomes the destination all return to.

topics.headline: fronted destination turns chosen return into inevitable endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the movement from wrong association with God to voluntary return to God and finally to exclusive return to God.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase is the fronted predicate of the nominal return sentence, and the repeated first-person phrase creates the local doublet.

words.gloss_range: your fixed return-point after the fronted divine destination, gathering prior choices into final accountability
words.prose: {{ar:مَرْجِعُكُمْ}} ({{tr:marjiʿukum}}) is the delayed subject after the fronted destination, so return is stated as a fixed endpoint rather than narrated as a passing event. The mīm-noun can press place and time of return, and the plural suffix makes it the addressees' own return; it also joins the return-and-informing pattern repeated in 31:23 and contrasts voluntary turning with inevitable return.
words.root_gloss_range: returning back to a place, state, point, or time; locally a mīm-prefixed return noun with plural possessive suffix

topics.headline: return noun fixes destination, timing, and accountability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that every prior movement in the ayah is gathered into a fixed return-point that belongs to the plural addressees.
topics.reason: The noun functions as subject of the nominal sentence after a fronted predicate; form and suffix evidence support a return point belonging to the addressees.

words.gloss_range: sequential and causal connector making disclosure follow immediately from return
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) closes the delayed-return movement with immediate disclosure. After the long interval marked by the previous sequence particle, this connector makes informing the direct consequence of arriving at the return point.

topics.headline: after delayed return, informing follows at once
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the coda's timing: life stretches toward return, but disclosure follows immediately once return is reached.
topics.reason: The connector links the return assertion to the informing verb in the sequenced coda.

words.gloss_range: first-person divine informing that makes deeds fully disclosed to the plural addressees after return
words.prose: {{ar:أُنَبِّئُكُمْ}} ({{tr:unabbiʾukum}}) shifts from the singular child scenario to plural divine disclosure. Form II makes the informing weighty and complete, while the root's news field makes deeds into a consequential report; the formulaic return-and-informing pattern is echoed in 31:23, and disclosure language also appears in wider divine-report formulas (3:15, 3:49).
words.root_gloss_range: news, consequential report, and disclosure; locally a Form II divine informing verb, not generic casual telling

topics.headline: God fully informs the plural addressees
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the family case has widened into universal accountability where God turns lived deeds into disclosed news.
topics.reason: The verb carries a first-person divine subject and plural object suffix after the immediate connector; Form II and root evidence support weighty disclosure while local grammar selects informing.

words.gloss_range: preposition introducing the content about which divine informing occurs
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) connects the informing verb to its report material. The disclosure is not merely that judgment exists; it concerns the lived content that the final relative clause will gather.

topics.headline: preposition opens the report material
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that deeds become the material of divine report, not a vague backdrop to judgment.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the following relative content phrase as complement of the informing verb.

words.gloss_range: open relative pronoun gathering all acted content under final disclosure
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) opens the final relative clause broadly. It does not preselect one class of deeds; it gathers whatever the addressees were doing into the scope of divine disclosure.

topics.headline: open relative gathers the record
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final report is comprehensive and ends the ayah on human doing rather than abstract judgment alone.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun is governed by the preposition as disclosure content and functions within the final action clause.

words.gloss_range: past being auxiliary framing the final deed verb as sustained habitual action
words.prose: {{ar:كُنْتُمْ}} ({{tr:kuntum}}) gives the final deed predicate past habitual depth. The root's being-field makes the disclosure concern what the addressees had come to be through repeated action, while the local construction keeps the word as the frame for the following imperfect verb.
words.root_gloss_range: being, existence, and becoming-state; locally a perfect auxiliary that gives the final action predicate temporal depth

topics.headline: being-frame gives deeds sustained past aspect
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that judgment concerns sustained patterns of action, not an isolated snapshot.
topics.reason: The verb combines with the following imperfect as a strongly licensed predicate construction; root pressure survives as being-state imagery without replacing the auxiliary function.

words.gloss_range: ongoing performed deeds that close the ayah as the content of divine disclosure
words.prose: {{ar:تَعْمَلُونَ}} ({{tr:taʿmalūna}}) completes the habitual construction and lets the ayah close on human action. The root targets deliberate performed deeds rather than accidental happenings, while Form I keeps the accounting broad; the recurring disclosure formula appears elsewhere with the same audit force (16:32, 29:55, 39:24), and the same-surah reckoning pattern returns in 31:23.
words.root_gloss_range: intentional work, deed, operative action, and produced conduct; locally broad Form I doing under the habitual past frame

topics.headline: final word lands on sustained deliberate action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the whole sequence ends not on abstract family tension but on the record of deliberate deeds.
topics.reason: The imperfect supplies the predicate of the prior being verb and closes the relative content clause governed by the disclosure preposition.
